answer_1.quote: Neural encoder-decoder models are used to learn simplification rewrites from monolingual corpora of complex and simple sentences.

answer_2.quote: These methods are often evaluated by comparing their output to gold-standard, human-generated simplifications, using standard metrics (e.g., token-level precision, recall, F1), machine translation metrics (e.g., BLEU), text simplification metrics (e.g. SARI which rewards copying words from the original sentence), and readability metrics (among which Flesch-Kincaid Grade and Flesch Reading Ease are most commonly used).

answer_4.quote: It is desirable that the output of the computational models is ultimately validated by human judges.
answer_4.guideline: The generated simplification is tested, approved, and evaluated by human practitioners.
